t: Founded in 1501 by the Sufi leader Ismail I, the Safavid Empire reunited Iran for the first time since the Mongol Ilkhanate.
By imposing Twelver Shia Islam it gave Iran its lasting religious identity and turned the Sunni-Shia divide into a frontier with the Ottomans.
Weak harem-raised shahs and religious intolerance left it open to an Afghan revolt; Isfahan fell in 1722 and the dynasty ended in 1736.
dyk: After surrendering Isfahan in 1722, Shah Sultan Husayn personally placed the crown on the head of the Afghan conqueror Mir Mahmud Hotak.
ev: Ismail I defeats the Aq Qoyunlu, seizes Tabriz and proclaims Twelver Shiism the state religion
Selim I's Ottoman guns and janissaries rout the Qizilbash cavalry at Chaldiran
Shah Abbas I's reformed army recovers Herat and Khorasan from the Uzbeks
Abbas I begins moving the Armenian merchants of Julfa to New Julfa beside Isfahan
Abbas I expels the Portuguese from Hormuz with English naval help
The Treaty of Zuhab fixes a Safavid-Ottoman frontier close to today's Iran-Iraq border
Mir Mahmud Hotak wins at Gulnabad and takes Isfahan after a seven-month siege
Nader Quli Afshar is proclaimed Shah on the Mughan plain, ending the Safavid dynasty
